part.text: {"program": [{"op": "reserve", "slot": 0}, {"op": "reserve", "slot": 1}, {"op": "read", "slot": 0, "src": 0}, {"op": "read", "slot": 1, "src": 1}, {"op": "wait_reads"}, {"op": "publish", "slot": 0}, {"op": "publish", "slot": 1}, {"op": "acquire", "slot": 0}, {"op": "acquire", "slot": 1}, {"op": "write", "slot": 0, "dst": 0}, {"op": "write", "slot": 1, "dst": 1}, {"op": "wait_writes"}, {"op": "release", "slot": 0}, {"op": "release", "slot": 1}], "rationale": "Third submission of the twice-accepted program, optimal on the lexicographic objective [2,14,2]. Waits=2 is the minimum: publish needs an initialized value with no pending read and release needs no pending transfer, so at least one wait_reads and one wait_writes are unavoidable. With waits fixed at 2, expected=[0,1] requires two distinct pages live simultaneously (peak-1 would force a second reserve/read cycle, i.e. 4 waits, losing the primary criterion), so each slot runs exactly reserve+read+publish+acquire+write+release = 6 commands, giving 12+2=14 commands minimum. Safety under arbitrary completion order: both reads are issued before the single blocking wait_reads, which drains the entire non-FIFO read queue, so both slots are initialized at every state where publish/acquire/write executes; writes target distinct destinations from distinct acquired slots, and the single blocking wait_writes drains all pending writes before either release. Final state: pc=end, no pending transfers, all slots free, dst0 origin 0 and dst1 origin 1 matching expected=[0,1]. Peak live slots = 2. No timing assumptions beyond DMA eventual-completion fairness; all interleavings are safe."}
